title: Concise FAQ Snippet Demotes the Real Approval Path
summary: The retriever finds the full shoreline-waiver procedure, but the reranker promotes a short FAQ snippet and an outdated policy. The correct signer falls below the packing cutoff, so the answer attributes final approval to the wrong role.
query: Who signs the final shoreline waiver after legal review?

dataset.name: Harbor permitting packet
dataset.notes: Synthetic permitting corpus with a procedure memo, FAQ, old policy, checklist, and internal email.

debugChecklist: Inspect whether reranking promotes short snippets that repeat the question without carrying the final role assignment.
Compare packed context against outdated policy documents that may mention a different signer.
If the correct procedural memo is already in the candidate set, test a no-rerank or larger-pack counterfactual before changing retrieval.

chunks.label: Procedure chunk 1
chunks.text: The operations chief assembles the waiver packet and sends it to legal for review once environmental exhibits are complete.

chunks.label: Procedure chunk 2
chunks.text: After legal review, the port director signs the final shoreline waiver. The operations chief signs only the routing sheet earlier in the process.

chunks.label: FAQ chunk 1
chunks.text: Legal review happens before final shoreline waiver approval, and operations prepares the packet for that review.

chunks.label: Archived policy chunk 1
chunks.text: Under the 2023 rule, the operations chief signed the final shoreline waiver after legal review.

chunks.label: Checklist chunk 1
chunks.text: Confirm that legal comments are closed and the port director signature block is ready before publishing the final waiver.

chunks.label: Email chunk 1
chunks.text: I only sign the routing sheet now; final waiver signatures moved to the port director when the 2025 procedure took effect.

runs.label: Baseline · reranker on

verdict.headline: The reranker favored a short FAQ and an outdated policy over the current procedure memo.
verdict.detail: The top packed chunks mention legal review and operations, but the sentence assigning the final signature to the port director gets pushed below the context budget.

runs.story: Phrase-heavy snippets and stale documents can beat the longer procedure even when retrieval already found the right evidence.
runs.outcome: The answer revives the old signer or attributes final approval to operations instead of the port director.
